addClaims.text: New apps start in development mode, usable by at most 5 authenticated Spotify users.
addClaims.quote: Up to 5 authenticated Spotify users can use an app that is in development mode

addClaims.text: Each development-mode user must be added to the app's allowlist first.
addClaims.quote: Each Spotify user who installs your app will need to be added to your app's allowlist before they can use it.

addClaims.text: The app owner needs a Spotify Premium account for development-mode apps to work.
addClaims.quote: The app owner must have a Spotify Premium account for apps in development mode to function.

addClaims.text: Since May 15, 2025 Spotify only accepts extended-quota applications from organizations, not individuals.
addClaims.quote: as of May 15th 2025, Spotify only accepts applications from organizations (not individuals)

addClaims.text: Extended quota requires an established business, a launched service and at least 250k monthly active users.
addClaims.quote: Maintaining a minimum of active users (at least 250k MAUs)

addClaims.text: Extended quota mode removes the allowlist and user limit and raises rate limits.
addClaims.quote: Apps in this category can be installed by an unlimited number of users and the allowlist in development mode no longer applies.

addClaims.text: Spotify says over 95% of extended-access applications fell short of its security, privacy and licensing standards.
addClaims.quote: over 95% of the applications we receive for extended Web API access fall short of basic security, privacy, and licensing standards

addClaims.text: localhost is not allowed as a redirect URI; use HTTPS, or an explicit loopback IP like http://127.0.0.1:PORT.
addClaims.quote: localhost is not allowed as redirect URI.

addClaims.text: Redirect URIs must use HTTPS unless they are a loopback address.
addClaims.quote: Use HTTPS for your redirect URI, unless you are using a loopback address, when HTTP is permitted.

addClaims.text: Requests for users not on the allowlist return a 403 error.
addClaims.quote: will receive a 403 status code error

addClaims.text: Composio does not manage an OAuth app for Spotify: toolkits.get("spotify") returns composioManagedAuthSchemes [] (auth modes: OAUTH2), so you bring your own.

verdict.label: Partner-only or paid / gated
verdict.summary: Building and testing is self-serve, but development mode caps you at 5 allowlisted users, and production (extended quota) is only for registered organizations with 250k+ monthly active users. For most agent builders, Spotify is effectively partner-only.
verdict.cost: Free API; app owner needs Spotify Premium

addRedirectRules.rule: Use HTTPS, or an explicit loopback IP (http://127.0.0.1:PORT or http://[::1]:PORT). The hostname localhost is rejected.

addBlockers.symptom: A 6th user (or anyone not allowlisted) gets 403 errors after connecting
addBlockers.cause: The app is in development mode: max 5 users, each on the allowlist.
addBlockers.fix: Add the user to the allowlist in the Developer Dashboard (if you have fewer than 5).
addBlockers.fallback: Apply for extended quota as an organization meeting the criteria; otherwise scope your product to single-user / personal use.

addBlockers.symptom: Dashboard rejects http://localhost:3000/callback as a redirect URI
addBlockers.cause: Spotify no longer allows the localhost hostname.
addBlockers.fix: Use http://127.0.0.1:3000/callback for local testing, and Composio's HTTPS callback for real connections.

replaceRequirements.label: 5 allowlisted users in development mode
replaceRequirements.when: Until Spotify moves the app to extended quota mode

replaceRequirements.label: Spotify Premium on the app owner's account

addUncertainties: Spotify does not publish a turnaround time for extended-quota applications; the production range is an estimate, and most individual developers will not qualify at all.
